full_judgment: 29. In the case of Bangladesh vs Fazle Karim reported in 42 DLR (AD) 91, it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that the presumption of service of public notice for acquisition of property being an official act, a presumption is available under the Evidence Act that it has been regularly performed unless the country is proved. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, provided that the Court may presume that the judicial and official acts have been regularly performed. Where once making to an order under a statute has been proved, there may well be presumption that it was duly made as required by law. Once the publications of the orders in the official Gazette are established the process of publications should be presumed to have been considered sufficient. Since the proceedings took place long ago the same must be presumed to be regular. Similarly, where the report states that symbolical possession is delivered, there is a presumption as to formalities having been complied with. Irregularity is not to be presumed, but a party alleging it may prove it. The writ petitioners did not take any step to rebut the presumption.
